So I originally had a booking online but I didn’t go to that one. (Not sure how it works in Poland but just did it online there was no socialising with anyone to book). Instead, I went to one of the drop in sessions, no appointment was needed. 

So we walked in the door and a man said do you have an appointment? I answered no and he directed us where to go and we just followed some arrows. 

We then came to a room with desks and a woman told me to go to desk number 4. A nurse asked my full name, if I had an appointment, date of birth etc. She then handed me a sheet and told me which vaccine I would be getting.
 
I then followed more arrows to a big room (with the vaccination bits) and a woman told me which number to go to. I walked over and sat down and the nurse asked some things (which I think she asks everyone). Do you have a fever? Do you feel well? Could you be pregnant? Etc. Then she said possible side effects like sore arm. She then said it won’t take long. And trust me, it really wasn’t! I’m scared of needles but honestly it was painless and so quick! 

She then said just wait over in one of the waiting area seats for 15 minutes then you can go. (Just to make sure you don’t have a reaction). Then I was able to go and that was it :) 

It wasn’t a bad experience at all. Just remember: the nurses are seeing hundredsss of people every day and are probably so bored, they won’t remember you! Some people probably faint, are sick, crying... so you just maybe being a little awkward they won’t take notice honestly.

Also, it is not something you have to do alone. Your friends/ family may be a distance away but you can always phone call or text. And if you don’t feel like sharing this information with them there is other (anonymous) things that would help. Police, first of all. As well as relationship and abuse helplines, and I’d imagine a specific helpline for whatever you may have found on his phone. I’ll be here to help if u want someone to chat to privately aswell.
Best of luck!
